record.paper_title: Progress and open questions in the physics of neutrino cross sections at intermediate energies
record.original_question: What dedicated neutrino or antineutrino scattering measurements on free or nearly free nucleons are needed to determine the nucleon axial structure directly, without the confounding nuclear-model uncertainties that affect measurements on nuclear targets?

evidence.quote: In fact, we think that dedicated (anti)neutrino-nucleon experiments are needed in order to understand the axial structure of the nucleon in depth.

artifact.category_tag: neutrino-nucleon scattering and axial form factor
artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the quasi-elastic charged-current process ν_ℓ + n → ℓ^- + p (and the antineutrino analogue ν̄_ℓ + p → ℓ^+ + n), the hadronic matrix element of the weak charged current between nucleon states is parametrized by vector form factors F_1(Q^2), F_2(Q^2) (fixed by electron scattering and CVC) and by an axial form factor F_A(Q^2) together with a pseudoscalar form factor F_P(Q^2) related to F_A by PCAC. The Q^2-dependence of F_A(Q^2), with normalization F_A(0) = g_A determined from neutron β-decay, encodes the axial structure of the nucleon (e.g. its axial mass M_A in a dipole ansatz, or model-independent z-expansion coefficients).

Existing extractions of F_A(Q^2) from (anti)neutrino scattering on nuclear targets (e.g. C, O, Ar, Fe) are confounded by nuclear-physics uncertainties: Fermi motion, binding, Pauli blocking, short- and long-range nucleon–nucleon correlations, multi-nucleon (2p2h) currents, final-state interactions, and pion-production backgrounds, which mix with the nucleon-level signal and bias the inferred F_A.

Problem. Specify a complete experimental programme of dedicated (anti)neutrino scattering measurements on free or nearly free nucleon targets (e.g. hydrogen, deuterium, or hydrogen-rich molecular targets with statistical or kinematic subtraction of bound-nucleon contributions) — including the choice of target, beam energy spectrum, detector capabilities, kinematic coverage in Q^2, and event selections — that suffices to determine the nucleon axial form factor F_A(Q^2) (and, where accessible, F_P(Q^2)) directly from the data, without recourse to a nuclear model. Demonstrate that the proposed programme can extract F_A(Q^2) over the Q^2 range relevant to accelerator-based oscillation experiments (roughly 0 ≤ Q^2 ≲ 3 GeV^2) with uncertainties dominated by statistics and well-controlled electroweak/QED corrections rather than by nuclear-model assumptions.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of obtaining a direct, nuclear-model-independent determination of the nucleon axial form factor via dedicated (anti)neutrino-nucleon experiments remains open. Proposals and ongoing efforts to perform measurements on hydrogen/deuterium-rich targets (e.g. the LDMX/MINERvA hydrogen analyses via transverse-kinematic-imbalance subtraction, and proposed high-pressure H_2 TPCs for DUNE near detectors) are under development but no comprehensive free-nucleon F_A(Q^2) extraction has yet been achieved; recent reviews continue to list this as an outstanding need.

status_evidence.title: Snowmass Neutrino Frontier Report on Neutrino Interaction Cross Sections
status_evidence.snippet: Highlights the lack of modern free-nucleon (anti)neutrino cross section data and identifies hydrogen/deuterium target measurements as a key need for axial form factor determination.
status_evidence.claim: Free-nucleon axial-structure measurements are still listed as an open experimental need.

status_evidence.title: MINERvA hydrogen-target antineutrino-proton analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Reports a first extraction of the axial form factor from antineutrino scattering on hydrogen using kinematic subtraction in CH, but with limited Q^2 reach and statistics.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists but a comprehensive free-nucleon programme is not yet realized.
